rich_summary: A grand martial exhibition is held to display the skills of the Kuru princes before the kingdom. Kings, nobles, and citizens gather around a magnificent arena as Drona presides over the tournament. One by one the princes demonstrate their mastery of weapons—archery, chariot driving, swordplay—astonishing the crowd. The tension rises when Bhima and Duryodhana enter the arena with maces, their rivalry stirring the spectators into divided factions until Ashwatthaman restrains them. Drona then dramatically presents Arjuna, his most beloved pupil. Arjuna appears in radiant armor and displays his prowess, causing the assembly to erupt in praise. Kunti is moved to tears at the acclaim for her son, while Dhritarashtra, hearing the uproar, asks the reason and is told that Arjuna has entered the arena. The scene elevates Arjuna as the foremost warrior and foreshadows the rivalries that will shape the epic.

highlight_spans.why: Opens the scene with the public spectacle atmosphere of the tournament.
The crowd compared to an 'agitated ocean' captures the massive excitement of the gathering.
Bhima and Duryodhana’s entrance with maces highlights the central rivalry between the Pandavas and Kauravas.
Drona publicly introduces Arjuna as his greatest pupil, marking Arjuna’s rise as the preeminent warrior.
Kunti’s emotional reaction—tears mixing with the milk of her breast—reveals the deep maternal pride and feeling surrounding Arjuna.

top_scenes.scene_text: The vast tournament arena filled with nobles and citizens as the princes ride and shoot arrows while drums and trumpets thunder.
Bhima and Duryodhana facing each other in the arena with raised maces, circling like enraged elephants as the crowd roars.
Arjuna enters in golden armor with bow and quiver, glowing like a sunset cloud as the entire assembly erupts in praise.
